title: How well the browser must work

entities.title: Repository content can't run
entities.summary: Text from a repository is never run as code.
entities.requirement: Everything read from a repository is escaped, and Markdown is rendered only as paragraphs, lists, bold, inline code and links; HTML in a file stays text, and a link with any scheme other than http, https or mailto keeps its words and loses its target.
entities.measuredBy: Reading md() and every place file content is written into the page; a file with HTML in its details shows the HTML as text.

entities.title: Usable from the keyboard
entities.summary: Tabs, parts and panels work without a pointer, in Flat and in Cyberspace.
entities.requirement: Tabs follow the ARIA tabs pattern with arrow keys, Home and End; every drawn part with something to show is focusable and opens with Enter or Space; Escape closes the inspector and the token panel; focus is outlined in the kind's colour. In Cyberspace, Tab walks a visually hidden list after the canvas, a button per part of the cities standing, per floor of the tower and per building of the skyline, each named after it: focusing one lights it (its focus ring, edges in --hot) and Enter does what a click does. On the canvas the arrow keys, + and − and F move the camera, ↑ and ↓ go from floor to floor in the tower, and in the street W A S D, Z, Space and the arrows walk wherever they can't mean something else. The inspector, panels and switch are ordinary HTML in tab order.
entities.measuredBy: Walking a folder with the keyboard alone. In Cyberspace, reaching and selecting every part of this repository's component city, every floor of its root tower, every building of its skyline and a part in the street with the keyboard alone (Chrome, 2026-11-15: 39 parts, 26 floors, 5 buildings).

entities.title: Respects reduced motion
entities.summary: With reduced motion on, nothing animates.
entities.requirement: When the system asks for reduced motion, the drill animation, pulses, flashes, the ticking square and the fades are off, and scrolling jumps. In Cyberspace every flight, slide and fade lands at once, and so does the view's turn toward a selection and its move to bring a part focused from the keyboard into view; walking still moves, because the reader drives it (decision cyberspace-motion).
entities.measuredBy: Turning on reduced motion in the system and walking a folder. In Cyberspace, counting the animation frames each move asks for with reduced motion emulated: 1 to 3 for every flight, slide, fade and refit (42 to 187 without it), and as many as without it while walking (Chrome, 2026-11-15); a selection in the city, turning toward its part, 2 with reduced motion against 65 without (2026-11-15).

entities.title: Light and dark
entities.summary: Every colour of Flat has a light and a dark value; Cyberspace is always dark.
entities.requirement: Every colour is a token with a value for light and one for dark, chosen by the system's setting, in Flat. Cyberspace is always dark (decision space-gibson-look): while it shows, the window takes the dark values and Cyberspace's own tokens, which have no light value, read by spaceTheme; leaving it, Flat follows the system again. Label text stands at least 4.5:1 against its pill over every part of Cyberspace's sky.
entities.measuredBy: Reading the :root tokens and their dark block; opening the page in both. For Cyberspace, test/space.test.js reads the dark block, its copy under :root.space and Cyberspace's tokens, and checks every pill; with the system in light mode, Cyberspace and the whole window are dark.

sources.symbol: label text stands 4.5:1 against its pill

entities.details: Until decision space-gibson-look Cyberspace followed the system too: a city re-themed both ways kept its geometries (15 before and after, 2026-11-15), and artboards 4 to 6 drew it in light mode.

entities.title: From a 15-inch laptop to a 34-inch monitor
entities.summary: Supported from a 15-inch screen; designed for 27-inch and 34-inch and wider monitors.
entities.requirement: Everything works on a 15-inch laptop screen, the smallest supported. The page is designed for 27-inch monitors and for 34-inch and wider ones, and makes good use of their width. Smaller screens, phones included, need not be supported.
entities.measuredBy: Opening a repository in a full browser window at about 1440 × 900 CSS pixels (a 15-inch laptop), 2560 × 1440 (27 inches) and 3440 × 1440 (34 inches, ultrawide).
entities.details: Cyberspace (plan cyberspace-mode, step 7): its panels keep their pixel sizes and the scene takes the rest of the window, so a wider screen gives the scene more room, never bigger panels; below 1280 px wide the Layers panel folds into a 40 px button that opens it as a popover and the legend shows its icons alone, their words as tooltips; below 900 px tall the street's map is 180 px wide. Checked in Chrome on 2026-11-15 in every scene at 1280 × 800, 1440 × 900, 2560 × 1440 and 3440 × 1440: no panel overlaps another or leaves the window. Flat is not yet laid out for the wider screens (limitation wide-screens-unused).

entities.title: Few requests
entities.summary: Listing costs two requests on GitHub, and files are read twelve at a time.
entities.requirement: Listing a GitHub repository takes two API calls, or one when the address names a branch, so a reader without a token can open about thirty repositories an hour; files are read twelve at a time; a drawing is laid out only when its tab opens.
entities.measuredBy: Counting requests in the browser's network panel.

entities.title: Degrades rather than fails
entities.summary: Without the fonts, the layout library, a file, WebGL or three.js, the rest still works.
entities.requirement: Without the web fonts the page uses system fonts and lays drawings out again if the fonts arrive late; without dagre it shows tables; a file that can't be read is skipped and named. Cyberspace never stands in the way of reading: without WebGL 2 or three.js a Cyberspace address shows Flat and the status line says why; without dagre, or where dagre can't lay a view out, the city stands on a grid and says so; a folder with no drawn views has a tower of floors to read and no city; a view the models can't build stays a floor whose inspector says why; a lost WebGL context offers Restore it, which builds the scene the address names again.
entities.measuredBy: Blocking jsDelivr, and adding a broken .dev file. For Cyberspace (Chrome, 2026-11-15): --disable-3d-apis; blocking three.js and dagre; a dagre that throws on one view; .github, which has no drawn views; a state diagram the models can't build; WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext(), then Restore it, and restoreContext().

entities.title: Cyberspace keeps up
entities.summary: Cyberspace draws a frame in 16 ms for this repository and 33 ms for 400 parts on an M1 MacBook Air, in at most 40 draw calls, opens within 1.5 s, and costs Flat nothing.
entities.requirement: On a 2021 MacBook Air (M1), a frame, from its start to the GPU finishing it, takes at most 16 ms for this repository and 33 ms for a city of 400 parts, while orbiting and walking, at 1440 × 900 and at 3440 × 1440 with device pixel ratio 2; on an M1 Pro, whose GPU is about twice as fast, half that. A city scene draws in at most 40 calls, its layers, a selection and a beam under the pointer included, and the skyline in at most 8. The first Cyberspace frame comes at most 1.5 s after the switch is pressed on a cold cache and 300 ms on a warm one. A page load in Flat fetches nothing for Cyberspace. Leaving for Flat lets go of every geometry, material and texture, and of the WebGL context a minute later.
entities.measuredBy: The ?spacestats readout (the frame time with gl.finish(), draw calls, renderer.info.memory and what is left on leaving), in Chrome for Testing driven through the DevTools protocol on an M1 Pro: a three-second drag for orbiting and W then A held for walking; Network.clearBrowserCache for a cold cache, the page loaded again for a warm one; the requests of a page load in Flat; GPU buffers, textures, programs and vertex arrays counted by wrapping WebGL2's create and delete calls over ten trips in and out; isContextLost() 61 s after leaving.
entities.details: Measured on 2026-11-15 on an M1 Pro (targets 8 and 16 ms), the readout's frame time averaged over a drag or a walk, its worst in brackets. This repository's component city (5 plates, 28 towers, 6 beacons, 40 beams): orbiting 0.42 ms (2.4) at 1440 × 900 and 0.34 ms (1.0) at 3440 × 1440; its street, Loader selected: orbiting 0.53 ms (1.3 and 1.6) and walking 0.39 ms (0.9) and 0.48 ms (1.9). The 400-part city of the branch perf/400-parts (36 plates, 352 towers, 12 beacons, 474 beams): orbiting 4.28 ms (5.8) and 3.91 ms (4.4); its street: orbiting 0.42 and 0.52 ms, walking 0.49 ms (1.8) and 0.39 ms (0.5). Walking, a frame came every 16.9 to 17.0 ms at both sizes: the display's 60 Hz. Draw calls: 10 for either city with nothing selected (15 for this repository's with Loader selected); 6 for retro-games' skyline of 93 buildings; this repository's component city with four more of its drawn views standing, 34, and 40 with Loader selected and a beam under the pointer; the Layers panel disables the tick box of a sixth, which would pass 40 (cityCalls, layerFits). The first frame after the address asks for Cyberspace, as the switch does: 203 to 247 ms to the root tower and 158 to 169 ms to the component city with Loader selected on a cold cache (three.js fetched from jsDelivr), 201 to 257 and 150 to 157 ms on a warm one, and 13 to 20 ms coming back within the minute. A page load in Flat: 59 requests, none of them for three.js. Leaving for Flat: 0 geometries and 0 textures in renderer.info.memory, and 0 GPU buffers, programs and vertex arrays (three.js's 4 default textures stay until the context goes), the same after each of ten trips through all four scenes, with the page's DOM nodes and listeners unchanged; the context was lost 61 s after leaving. The panels' backdrop-filter blur at 3440 × 1440, device pixel ratio 2, walking with the inspector open: every frame 16.7 ms with it and without it, so it stays.
